name: Cloudflare Agents
tagline: An SDK for building stateful AI agents on Cloudflare Workers.
hook: Separates SDK tests, browser hook tests, and type tests, with a coverage matrix mapping features to CI evidence.
summary: Cloudflare Agents gives packages, examples, tutorials, and design records their own local instructions. The root guide explains the split between runtime and browser tests, generated bindings, and public package releases.

techniques.title: Route by the purpose of a directory
techniques.body: The nested-guide table separates SDK internals from examples, narrative tutorials, user documentation, and design records. The routing carries writing and consistency expectations as well as code conventions.
techniques.quote: Some directories have their own AGENTS.md with deeper guidance:

techniques.title: Distinguish runtime tests from browser hook tests
techniques.body: Workers tests run in the Workers pool, while React hooks use a separate Playwright-based command and directory. The guide also points to a coverage matrix that maps features to layers and CI evidence.
techniques.quote:
pnpm run test             # agents + ai-chat unit/integration tests
pnpm run test:react       # Playwright-based React hook tests (agents package)

techniques.title: Name the generator for environment types
techniques.body: Environment declaration files must be regenerated inside the relevant package or example. The command and working directory matter because bindings are scoped to that configuration.
techniques.quote: `env.d.ts` files are generated by `wrangler types` — regenerate with `pnpm exec wrangler types` inside the relevant example/package, don't hand-edit

techniques.title: Keep published behavior distinct from learning material
techniques.body: Public API and bug-fix changes in packages need changesets. Examples, guides, and sites do not, so the rule follows what is released to package consumers.
techniques.quote: Examples, guides, and sites don't need changesets.

steal: Route documentation and examples by their purpose, not just their file type.
State which tests exercise the actual runtime and which require a browser.
Put the generator and working directory beside generated-file restrictions.
Base release-note requirements on the published surface.
